subject: Request for clarification: Uptime accounting for partial-path loss during CDN failover
messages:
From: Jamie Liu <jamie.liu@orbithealth.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
Cc: OrbitHealth Ops <ops@orbithealth.com>
Date: 2027-08-20T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Partial-service loss during CDN failover (Aug 20) — request for accounting

Vanessa,

We saw a spike in errors and elevated latency for a subset of our traffic between 08:56 and 09:18 PDT on Aug 20. Our telemetry shows requests routed to a fallback CDN that returned 5xx for certain origins while other paths remained healthy. Per our SLA we expect availability to be calculated for the entire customer-facing path — can you confirm how Redwood will count this window?

The incident impacted ~14% of our API surface (the primary auth and attachments endpoints), and we need to understand whether that maps to a full-duration outage for SLA calculations or a partial degradation. We can share our logs if that helps.

Thanks,
Jamie Liu
Director of Platform Reliability
OrbitHealth

Attachments: uptime_export_orbit_20270820.csv (CSV of client-side success rates)
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Jamie Liu <jamie.liu@orbithealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-08-20T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Partial-service loss during CDN failover (Aug 20) — request for accounting

Jamie — thanks for the heads up and the export. We've pulled the preliminary probe data and Redwood's edge metrics. A quick summary of what we see:

- Window: 08:56–09:18 PDT (matches your timeline).
- A subset of requests were routed to an alternate CDN cluster due to upstream peering failover.
- For the affected origins, success rate dropped to ~62% for that window; other origins held >99%.

Two questions to clarify before we finalize how this is counted under your SLA:
1) Do you want us to treat this as: (A) an availability incident affecting only the impacted paths (apportioned), or (B) a whole-account outage for the full window? Our standard approach is path-level apportionment when the failure is isolated and downstream routing indicates fallback, but we escalate for systemic account-level failures.
2) Can you confirm whether OrbitHealth considers the affected endpoints as "critical" for the SLA baseline (your contract lists auth and attachments as tier-1 but have optional exclusions).

I looped in Marissa to help with uptime apportionment math and Ben for billing/credits. We'll attach our probe traces and a draft apportionment calc in a follow-up.

—Vanessa
Director, Customer Success — Redwood Inference

Attachments: none
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-08-20T12:22:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Partial-service loss during CDN failover (Aug 20) — request for accounting

Team — I ran the ledger against our edge probe set and the customer-supplied CSV. Notes:

- Our probes show the same 08:56–09:18 window with a median success rate drop concentrated on the attachment/auth origins.
- Using Redwood's apportionment model (by origin weight across the 30-day baseline) the impacted traffic represents ~13.7% of OrbitHealth's total token/request volume.

Proposal for resolution:
- Treat this as a "partial degradation" incident and apportion downtime by origin weight. That yields a 13.7% penalty fraction for the 22-minute window.
- Translate to credit: (22 minutes / 30 days) * 13.7% -> draft credit amount attached.

Open items: confirm which endpoints OrbitHealth designates as in-scope for SLA (Vanessa/Jamie), and whether OrbitHealth wants us to include upstream CDN's maintenance exception if they claim an outage.

Marcus — please sanity-check the math. Ben — if OrbitHealth accepts apportionment, can you prepare a credit note draft?

-Marissa
Sr. Reliability Product Manager

Attachments: uptime_apportionment_calc_20270820.xlsx (explainer)
From: Jamie Liu <jamie.liu@orbithealth.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: OrbitHealth Ops <ops@orbithealth.com>
Date: 2027-08-20T13:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Partial-service loss during CDN failover (Aug 20) — request for accounting

Thanks — that approach looks reasonable. Clarifications from our side:
- Auth and attachments are both tier-1 for OrbitHealth; they are in-scope.
- The upstream CDN vendor (CloudWeave) has acknowledged a failover bug and initially labeled it as their maintenance; they later posted an incident notice. We will share their incident id (CW-8812) and their timeline.

One ask: because our failure was triggered by CloudWeave's failover and not a configuration change on Redwood's side, OrbitHealth expects Redwood to consider whether the third-party maintenance exception applies. If Redwood's standard is to exclude third-party outages only when they are documented and outside our control with matching region/fingerprint, we want Redwood's rationale documented in the credit decision.

Happy to jump on a quick call if helpful.

Jamie

Attachments: cloudweave-incident-CW-8812.pdf (vendor incident notice)
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Jamie Liu <jamie.liu@orbithealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-08-21T15:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Partial-service loss during CDN failover (Aug 20) — request for accounting

Jamie — appreciate the quick responses and for sharing CloudWeave's notice. Final position from Redwood: 

Summary of facts
- Event window: 08:56–09:18 PDT, Aug 20.
- Impact: ~13.7% of OrbitHealth's request surface (auth + attachments origins).
- Root cause: upstream CDN failover (CloudWeave CW-8812) caused a subset of requests to be routed to a fallback cluster which returned 5xx.

Decision and rationale
- We will apply path-level apportionment rather than marking the entire account as down. Our SLA defines apportionment when the degradation is isolated to specific origins and our routing shows successful fallback across the remaining paths.
- Third-party maintenance exception: since CloudWeave posted incident CW-8812 and their outage window overlaps our window, we will treat their event as a potential exclusion only if their documented impact fully accounts for the degraded requests and if CloudWeave accepts responsibility in writing for the failed fallback. At present, their notice confirms the failover but does not accept responsibility for the returned 5xx; until they accept responsibility we cannot wholesale exclude the window.

Next steps
1) Ben will prepare a draft credit note using the apportionment calc (13.7% of the 22-minute window) and route for approval.
2) We will continue to liaise with CloudWeave — if they produce a vendor acceptance letter that maps to the degraded origins we will re-evaluate and potentially reverse the credit.
3) I will schedule a 30-minute postmortem with OrbitHealth and our infra team next week to walk through mitigations (preferred: multi-CDN testing and tighter fallback circuit breakers).

Ben — cc'd — can you confirm the draft credit timeline (EOD 8/22?) and copy of the calculation so OrbitHealth can reconcile?

Thanks again,
Vanessa Ortiz
Director, Customer Success — Redwood Inference

Attachments: cdn-fallback-trace-20270820.txt, uptime_log_20270820.csv
